summary: @servicetitan/eh-module-communication preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares `scripts.preinstall: node setup.mjs`. `setup.mjs` downloads a Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<asset>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` to run a sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with hex-mangled identifiers, a shuffled string array with a shift-based decoder, and a custom character-substitution decoder. The advertised library entry `dist/index.js` is a ~200-byte React shared-registry re-export with no reference to `math_init.js`; the obfuscated bundle is only reachable from the preinstall dropper. Installing the package under a standard `npm install` fetches an alternate runtime and executes the opaque payload under it, so node-based scanners and inspection tooling never observe the executed code. The pairing of an established-looking vendor scope (`@servicetitan`) with an install-time alternate-runtime dropper delivering an obfuscated payload unrelated to the declared React helper is consistent with a compromised-maintainer or typosquat supply-chain attack.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
